He built a huge business from nothing. He still left with no cushion.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of a man who started with nothing, flipping pizzas and living in his mother-in-law's basement. The business exploded, and he kept hiring more people and building more buildings.

Kevin urged him to calm down, take some money out and set it aside, because a business does not climb forever. When it dipped, his fixed overhead was too high and the company went under. The problem, Kevin says, was that he never took any money out.

When did you last put something aside for slower days?
